chapter_theme: Knowledge comes from possessing grace (அருளுடைமையின் ஞானம் வருதல்): the Lord's grace is the source of good wealth, knowledge, greatness and divinity; it keeps deeds from clinging, removes birth and makes the soul one with Siva, and it is to be won in embodied life. Tirumular ends by vowing not to let go of Nandi until release.
structure_note: Litanies on what grace gives (1645, 1649, 1650), verses on merit and sin and the end of birth (1647, 1648), images of the soul taking on what it faces (the chariots in 1651, the sun- and moonstones in 1653), and a closing first-person vow (1654).

1645.reading: If the Lord's grace is there, good wealth is there; if the Lord's grace is there, good knowledge is there; in the Lord's grace there is greatness, and in the Lord's grace one becomes the great deity.
1645.nuance: The last line, பெருந்தெய்வமும் ஆமே, can mean that grace makes one divine or that the great God himself is reached in it. The chapter title borrows the Kural's chapter name அருளுடைமை but means the Lord's grace, not compassion between beings.

1646.reading: People wander the world as if spitting out the knowledge that spread across the five Tamil lands; yet the loosening mind, the knowledge of our Primal One and the five Tamil lands are all tattva.
1646.nuance: தமிழ் மண்டலம் ஐந்து is usually taken as the five Tamil regions, where the teaching spread; some read the five mandalas yogically, as regions of the body. உமிழ்வது போல (as if spitting out) may mean rejecting the knowledge or pouring it out. The verse's claim that all of it is tattva is clear; its tone toward the wanderers is not.

1647.reading: Merit and sin are two that come with one to the earth, and a few knowers see this when it happens; weigh them, cut both at the root, and seek out the Lord's dwelling beyond them.
1647.nuance: The verse asks for both merit and sin to be uprooted, since both bind to birth; it does not rank merit above sin. தப்பு அப்புறத்து is read as 'beyond, escaping both'.

1648.reading: Grace that goes before at the time of ending stands in the world as the life at the centre; grace that stays behind removes birth; standing before me, it gave me a release.
1648.nuance: The subject, grace, is supplied from the chapter; the verse names only what 'stands before' and 'stands behind'. முடிகின்ற காலம் may be death, the dissolution of the world or the end of a soul's bonds, and நடுவுயிர் may be the life within all or the soul held between births.

1649.reading: By Siva's grace some become gods, by Siva's grace some equal the deity, by Siva's grace deeds do not cling, and if Siva's grace is joined, that is Siva's world.
1649.nuance: The grades (gods, equal to the deity, free of deeds, Siva's world) mount toward the last, which makes Sivaloka not a place reached after death but the state of being joined to grace.

1650.reading: Drawing near the paired feet of the meritorious one, our father, the pure one, knowledge grew like a lamp; becoming one of earth or one of heaven happens only when one receives the Lord's grace.
1650.nuance: விளக்கென ஞானம் விளைந்தது, knowledge grew like a lamp, ties the chapter's title to an image. The last two lines put even ordinary human and heavenly births under grace, not only release. The father (எந்தை) may be Siva or the guru.

1651.reading: Mounting the chariot of the body, driven by the mind as charioteer, one mounts the chariot of maya and is bewildered; know these; mounting the chariot of love and receiving the stainless one's grace, one mounts the chariot of the assembly, and He becomes this one.
1651.nuance: The image of the body as chariot and the mind as charioteer is old (it is in the Katha Upanishad). Tirumular stacks four chariots: body, maya, love (நேயம்) and ஆயம், which may be the assembly of the Lord's company or the tattvas brought under control. அவன் இவன் ஆமே, 'He becomes this one', is traditionally the soul's union with Siva.

1652.reading: If one is born in that world with a body, it is in that world that one seeks those of rare tapas, in that world that one joins Hara's feet, and in that world that one receives grace.
1652.nuance: அவ்வுலகம், that world, is not named; it may be this earth, stressing that grace is won in embodied life, or a higher world in which one is reborn. The repetition makes the embodied birth the condition for every step that follows.

1653.reading: The sunstone that sees the sun takes the form of fire, the moonstone that sees the moon takes the form of clear water, the witness that holds the spark takes the form of flame, and the Lord who holds the fire takes on beautiful form.
1653.nuance: The sunstone and moonstone each take on the nature of what they face, and tradition reads the soul as taking on Siva's form when it faces him by grace. சதிகொண்ட சாக்கி is obscure: சாக்கி may be sakshi, the witnessing soul, or a flint (as in சக்கிமுக்கி); the last line may also mean that Siva, who holds fire, shines in the soul so lit.

1654.reading: Seeking him with all kinship, I search for our Nandi; having searched, I join him as Siva Peruman; having joined, so as to reach his sounding anklets, I do not let go until release.
1654.nuance: நாடும் உறவும் கலந்து can be 'with seeking and kinship mixed' or 'mingling land and kin', i.e. while still living among one's people. The chain தேடுவன், தேடி; கூடுவன், கூடி links each step to the next, and the verse ends on a clinging that is itself the way to release.

links.note: Both make அருள் the wealth above wealth. The Kural's அருள் is compassion toward living beings, and its chapter is named அருளுடைமை; Tirumular takes the same chapter name for the Lord's grace, the source of wealth, knowledge and divinity.
1625 says that only those with the Lord's grace know what tapas is; 1645 widens the claim: knowledge of every kind, with wealth and greatness, comes from grace.

Both say that both kinds of deed, good as well as bad, must cease to cling, and both tie this to the Lord: the Kural to those who love his true praise, Tirumular to seeking his dwelling beyond the two.
The Kural says cling to the one without clinging in order to let clinging go; Tirumular vows not to let go of Nandi until release, a clinging that is the way out.

source_issues: 1653 line 3 (சதிகொண்ட சாக்கி) is obscure and may be corrupt.
